sources.title: Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic
sources.note: Established 12 March 1922; All-Caucasian Congress 13 December 1922; founding member of the USSR 30 December 1922; area 186,043 km2 (no year); dissolved 5 December 1936; Adjar ASSR 16 July 1921; Abkhazia ASSR 19 February 1931; Nakhchivan July 1920.

sources.title: Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: Soviet Georgia from 25 February 1921; part of the TSFSR from 12 March 1922 to 5 December 1936; cession of the Artvin Okrug to Turkey; union republic 1936.

sources.title: Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: 28 April 1920; union of 12 March 1922; December 1936 dismantled.

notes: No Cliopatria row: the land is drawn inside Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes (1922-1991). Model: the federation is the federal layer; the Georgian, Armenian and Azerbaijan SSR dossiers each cede their whole country to it in March 1922 and take it back in December 1936, so the republics reappear as union republics without a second founding. Dates: the TSFSR page gives "Established: 12 March 1922" and, in the text, a transformation into a federal state by the First All-Caucasian Congress of Soviets on 13 December 1922 and USSR membership on 30 December 1922; the Armenian page gives 30 December 1922 as the date of joining; the ledger uses 12 March 1922, which two pages give. Area: gazetteer 181,835 km2 against 186,043 km2 (no year). Not on any page opened: the dates of the Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast (the Azerbaijan page is silent) and of the Zangezur settlement, so the internal Armenian-Azerbaijani line is the modern one. Abkhazia (treaty republic status from 16 December 1921, downgraded to an ASSR of the Georgian SSR 19 February 1931), South Ossetia (AO) and the Adjar ASSR (16 July 1921) were units inside the Georgian SSR, not drawn separately. The Transcaucasian federation is the only state of this region that held its land for under fifteen years; the three SSRs outlast it.
